title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding pages work with a set J of base points (for example rational or tangential points of a curve) and the fundamental groupoid Pi_1 with object set J. A group G' acts on Pi_1, and an extension E' of G' by pi_1 acts on the 'universal covers' X~'(J), the fibres of the universal covering over the base points. The previous page rebuilt the groupoid Pi_1 from the right pi_1-torsors X~'(j): Isom(j,j') = Isom_{pi_1}(X~'(j), X~'(j')). It then began rebuilding the action of g in G' using the pi_1-bitorsor B_g, the fibre of E' over g, via X~'(gj) = X~'(j) wedge_{pi_1} B_g.

This page has two parts.

1. Closing the previous argument. Contracting with B_g gives the map Isom_{pi_1}(X~'(j), X~'(j')) -> Isom_{pi_1}(X~'(gj), X~'(gj')). Grothendieck notes it would remain to show how his relations (7) and (8) follow from the single datum of the E'-action on X~'(J). That action restricts to a free action of pi_1 on X~'(J), whose quotient is J.

2. 'Reformulation': a general equivalence of categories.
- Category C has as objects the systems (1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1, Z), where Z is a nonempty E-set on which pi acts freely.
- Category C' has as objects the systems (Pi, Pi~, p, G, u), where Pi is a connected groupoid, p: Pi~ -> Pi is a universal covering, and u: G -> Aut(Pi) is an action by (strict) automorphisms.
- He announces mutually quasi-inverse equivalences alpha: C -> C' and beta: C' -> C.

Alpha is constructed on the next page.
- Pi is the gauge (Ehresmann) groupoid of the free pi-set Z -> Z/pi. Its objects are J = Z/pi, and Isom(j,j') = Isom_pi(Z_j, Z_j').
- Pi~ is the indiscrete (codiscrete) groupoid on Z, i.e. exactly one arrow between any two points. It is fibred discretely over Pi via the functor F(j) = Z_j, so Pi~ = Pi/F and Pi = Pi~/pi is an orbit groupoid.
- E acts on Pi~ through its action on Z. Since pi is normal, G = E/pi acts on the quotient Pi.

The inverse beta (implicit) goes as follows.
- pi is the deck group Aut(Pi~/Pi), which is isomorphic to the vertex groups of Pi; Z = Ob Pi~.
- E is the group of pairs (g, phi), where phi is an automorphism of Pi~ with p∘phi = u(g)∘p. Such lifts exist because Pi~ is simply connected, and they form a torsor under the deck group, so E is an extension of G by pi.

Mathematically this is the many-base-point (groupoid) form of the classical dictionary between group extensions 1 -> pi -> E -> G -> 1 and actions of G on the fundamental groupoid with a G-stable set of base points. It is the algebraic skeleton of how a Galois or symmetry group acts on pi_1 of a curve with several base points.
errors: Morphisms of C and C' are not specified. For an equivalence one must take morphisms in C' to include a compatible map of universal covers, since lifts are not unique; otherwise alpha is not fully faithful.

'Universal covering' must mean a covering with Pi~ simply connected, i.e. an indiscrete groupoid. The next page's phrase 'cat. discrète sur Pi' means 'discretely fibred over Pi', not a discrete category. The text itself has Isom(z,z') a single point.

u must be an action by strict automorphisms of Pi (an actual homomorphism to Aut(Pi), not to the 2-group of autoequivalences) for E to be recovered as a group of lifts. This is implicit but necessary.
The step '(7),(8) follow from the E'-action' is left explicitly undone ('Il faudrait encore expliciter...'). The reformulation is meant to replace it.

ideas.what: Reconstructing the action of g in G' on the fundamental groupoid by contracting the torsors X~'(j) with the bitorsor B_g = fibre of E' over g.
ideas.modern_name: Contracted product of torsors with a bitorsor; outer action via bitorsors
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 / Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne (bitorsor formalism); used implicitly in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Equivalence between (group extension of G by pi + nonempty E-set with free pi-action) and (connected groupoid with universal cover + G-action).
ideas.modern_name: Gauge groupoid / orbit groupoid of a principal pi-set; groupoid version of the extension–outer action dictionary; covering-groupoid theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann (gauge groupoid); R. Brown, P. J. Higgins (covering and orbit groupoids, 1960s–70s)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA 1 Exp. V (fundamental groupoid with several base points) and Esquisse d'un programme (fundamental groupoids with base-point sets stable under Galois); this exact equivalence statement: unsure

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard reformulation: G-equivariant connected groupoids with a universal cover correspond to group extensions with a free E-set. This is folklore in covering-groupoid theory and implicit in the later literature on Galois actions on fundamental groupoids with many base points (e.g. Deligne 1989, Ihara). Nothing here appears new; it shows Grothendieck setting up the groupoid framework for anabelian 'paradigms' of curves.
transcription_corrections: 'Z' is written as a script letter (likely \mathcal{Z} or a gothic Z).
Notation should be $\tilde{\mathcal{X}}'(J)$ (script X) as on the previous page, not $\tilde{X}'(J)$.
'(ayant J comme un quotient[?])' — likely 'ayant J comme ensemble quotient'.
'opérant sur Π par automorphismes' — the first struck 'sur' is a deletion; the reading is otherwise correct.
